title: Sign-out invalidates the project session; Keycloak session-end is an operator-declared option
description: A POST to the project's sign-out route invalidates the project session handle server-side and clears the session cookie (opaque-handle mode) or clears the bearer-source cookie (stateless mode); the next request from the browser is unauthenticated regardless of what the realm still holds. Provider-side sign-out through the realm's `end_session_endpoint` (RP-Initiated Logout, OIDC section) is NOT mandated: a realm record whose `providerLogout` field is `'redirect'` and whose `end_session_endpoint` is present on the discovery record causes the sign-out response to return a 302 to that endpoint after clearing the project session, with the `id_token_hint` query parameter carrying the raw id_token stored on the session record (opaque-handle mode) or the id_token the operator's declared bearer source has produced (stateless mode). A record that sets `providerLogout: 'redirect'` on a realm whose discovery omits `end_session_endpoint` is refused at boot with a stable-coded error naming the realm slug.
rationale: The project-session invariant is `sign-out clears the project session`; RP-initiated logout is a legitimate but variable operator preference (some deployments want a full realm sign-out, others want the realm session to persist for the operator's other applications on the same realm). Declaring the posture on the realm record with a fail-fast on missing endpoint catches misconfiguration where the project believes it is signing out at the realm and silently is not.
